messages:
jessica: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we need a small design for per-customer precision guarantees. customers want an SLA on max BLEU/EM/perf regressions when we switch to lower-bit profiles. thinking out loud: a 'quality escrow' concept that budgets acceptable degradation per request/customer. thoughts?

omar: High level: interesting. how do you see escrow being enforced at runtime? policy + telemetry or precomputed per-model/per-dataset thresholds?

jessica: Both. precompute profile->degradation curves via offline evals per model and a small calibration set per customer. runtime checks compare predicted degradation (from quick proxy) to remaining escrow budget; if exceed, fallback to higher-precision variant.

liam: Important: proxies must be cheap. otherwise we kill latency. propose a tiny classifier on prompt features + prefix token stats that estimates quality delta. 10-20ms budget.

anya: Also store escrow as tokens or percentage? e.g., customer allocated 1% quality-degradation/month or 1M tokens of 'degraded' output. which makes billing/alerting easier?

jessica: Prefer "degradation units" exposed in console. UI shows spend. Example: 1 unit = 0.1% expected metric drop on our calibration set. rounding/aggregation is an implementation detail.

omar: Edge case: open-ended generation where metric proxies (BLEU/ROUGE) break. Need a fallback safe mode: if proxy uncertain, conservatively not use low-bit. Could be a calibrated uncertainty threshold.

liam: Agree. Implement as: proxy returns (delta_estimate, uncertainty). If uncertainty > U_max or delta_estimate > remaining_escrow -> route to FP8/INT8 higher variant or dedicated high-safety pool.

anya: How to persist per-customer calibration? We should allow customers to upload a small eval set (10-50 prompts) for better accuracy, else use our default workload profile. store as human-readable JSON and keep a hash for audit.

jessica: Draft runtime policy (pseudo-JSON):
```json
{
  "policy_version": "0.1",
  "customer_id": "cust-123",
  "escrow_units": 1000,
  "profiles": [
    {"name": "fp8-fast", "expected_delta": 0.6, "uncertainty": 0.2, "cost_saving": 0.45},
    {"name": "int8-safe", "expected_delta": 0.2, "uncertainty": 0.05, "cost_saving": 0.25}
  ],
  "routing": {
    "on_high_uncertainty": "fallthrough_high_precision",
    "on_over_budget": "route_to_int8_if_available_else_high_precision"
  }
}
```

eva: Nice. A few operational notes:
- We need telemetry that links escrow spend to user-visible quality alerts (diffs on calibration set).
- Rollbacks: if observed quality drift > threshold, auto-pause all low-bit routes and notify SRE/product.
- Audit: every time escrow is consumed, create a compact record: (ts, request_id, profile, delta_estimate, uncertainty, units_charged).

omar: Performance routing: where do we evaluate proxy? sidecar in the serving process or separate lightweight service? Sidecar avoids extra network hop but tight CPU budget on GPUs machines. Separate service adds latency on cold paths. maybe allow both depending on deployment (hosted vs dedicated).

liam: We can make proxy pluggable in config per deployment. default: sidecar for hosted with small CPU cap; for Dedicated allow option to offload to routing service. Add a warm cache for recent prompts to skip proxy.

anya: How about experiments: can we allow controlled percentage of requests to draw from escrow automatically (like A/B)? e.g., spend 10% of escrow allowing more aggressive fp8 for a subset to gather real traffic signal.

jessica: Yes — add a canary mode in policy: "canary_alloc_pct": 5, and canary rules that prefer low-bit while charging at a multiplier so we learn impact faster.

runtime-bot: deploy scheduled: precision-proxy v0.2 -> staging at 2026-04-01T02:00Z :rocket:

omar: One more: billing + legal. If we allow quality escrow to be spent, customers might dispute. need explicit opt-in on contract and a dashboard export with examples. legal + sales to own language.

eva: I'll add audit export endpoints. product should define UI copy and default conservative settings.

jessica: Next steps: 1) prototype proxy (liam) 2) offline calibration harness (anya) 3) policy schema v0.1 + telemetry events (eva) 4) integration doc for hosted vs dedicated (omar). I'll open tickets.

liam: I'll spike the proxy this week, will post perf numbers.

anya: I'll draft the minimal calibration format and upload example.

omar: I'll write the routing config options and where to place the proxy.

jessica: Thanks everyone. If we agree on this approach I'll fold into the RFC follow-up and add an ops-runbook for pause/rollback. :thumbsup:
